chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jamila, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh! You have taken a seat that none sits in except a Prophet, a successor of a Prophet, or a wretch (oppressor).'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — the title of Imam Ali (AS), emphasizing his unique authority
key_terms.شَقِيٌّ: A wretch/oppressor (shaqiyy) — one destined for misery, here specifically one who usurps authority belonging to the Prophet or Imam
key_terms.مَجْلِساً: A seat/position of authority (majlis) — specifically the judicial seat/position of judge
key_terms.وَصِيُّ نَبِيٍّ: Successor of a Prophet (wasiyy al-nabi) — in Shia theology, this refers specifically to the divinely-appointed Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about who is qualified to be a judge in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) admonished Shurayh al-Qadi, the famous judge of Kufa appointed by Caliph Umar, warning him that the position of judge is so grave that it can only legitimately be held by a Prophet or a divinely-appointed successor (Imam). Shurayh accepted the judgeship under the Umayyad caliphs, and this narration reflects the Shia theological position that judicial and governing authority belongs exclusively to the Imam. Anyone else who assumes this authority — including judges appointed by non-Imams — falls into the category of the 'wretched' (shaqiyy), a term that in this context implies spiritual and moral ruin due to usurping a divinely-mandated role.
